stem: A 75-year-old client arrived at the outpatient clinic for an annual visit. Which of the following actions should the nurse take?

opts.t: Listen to the client reminisce about the stages of their life and critique accordingly.
Discourage the client from repetition while reminiscing about their lifespan.
Use open-ended questions to encourage the client to reminisce.
Teach the client to reminisce in an orderly fashion.
opts.why: Recall need not follow a strict order

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): C — Open-ended reminiscence supports recall; avoid criticism or rigid structure.

stem: When a nurse is providing care for a client who has been diagnosed with rubella, the nurse should implement which precaution method?

opts.t: Airborne
Contact
Droplet

ans: EXPECTED ANSWER (not keyed in source): C — Rubella requires droplet precautions.

stem: The nurse is providing care for a client who has scabies.  Which of the following is appropriate when providing care to this client?

opts.t: Wear gloves when entering the room
Wear a mask when within 3 feet of this client
opts.why: Routine mask does not prevent skin transmission

opts.t: Place a mask on the client when taking them to X-Ray
opts.why: Transport mask is not needed for scabies

opts.t: Permit no pregnant visitors
opts.why: Pregnancy alone is not a reason to exclude visitors

ans: EXPECTED ANSWER (not keyed in source): A — Scabies spreads by contact; gloves and gown.

stem: The nursing instructor is teaching a group of nursing students about how to prevent the spread of influenza. The nursing instructor identifies further teaching is necessary when a student states,

opts.t: “I will limit the amount of supplies that I bring into the client’s room.”
“The client should wear a mask if he/she must leave the room.”
“Hand hygiene must consist of soap and water in order to kill the influenza microorganism.”
opts.why: Alcohol rub is also effective if hands are not visibly dirty

opts.t: “I will wear gloves, gown, and mask when I enter the room to perform a physical assessment on the client.”

ans: EXPECTED ANSWER (not keyed in source): C — Alcohol hand rub is effective unless visibly soiled.

stem: The nurse is caring for a client diagnosed with Clostridium difficile (C. diff). To prevent the transmission of C. diff, the nurse should:

opts.t: perform hand hygiene with soap and water rather than alcohol based hand sanitizer.
assume that only surfaces that the client has touched are actually contaminated.
opts.why: Untouched surfaces may also be contaminated

opts.t: sterilize all of the equipment and supplies that leave the client’s room.
opts.why: Appropriate sporicidal disinfection is needed, not universal sterilization

opts.t: wear a mask when in the room and for the client to wear a mask when in public.

ans: EXPECTED ANSWER (not keyed in source): A — Soap and water physically remove spores.

stem: The nurse is teaching a new group of unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP) about the importance of hand hygiene. Which of the following statements should the nurse include?

opts.t: “If you don’t have an infection, your hands won’t infect others.”
“Use an alcohol rub when your hands are visibly soiled.”
opts.why: Visible soil requires soap and water

opts.t: “Rub all surfaces of your hands with an alcohol rub for 20 to 30 seconds.”
“If you wear gloves, you do not have to wash your hands.”
opts.why: Gloves do not replace hand hygiene

ans: EXPECTED ANSWER (not keyed in source): C — Rub all surfaces for 20–30 seconds; gloves do not replace hygiene.

stem: A nurse is observing an unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP) change the linens of a client's bed.  Which of the following observations requires follow-up?

opts.t: The UAP raises the bed to waist level
The UAP reaches across the bed to straighten the fitted sheet.
The UAP lowers the side rail on the side closest to them.
opts.why: Allows access while working at bedside

opts.t: The UAP rolls the client back and forth from one side of the bed to the other to make access easier
opts.why: Turning the client allows linen placement if done safely

ans: EXPECTED ANSWER (not keyed in source): B — Reaching across bed strains the back.

stem: The nurse preceptor is observing a new nurse wash their hands.  Which of the following, if observed, would require the preceptor to intervene?

opts.t: The nurse scrubs in circular motions using lots of friction
The nurse washes their hands for 15-20 seconds and sings Happy Birthday to themselves twice to ensure adequate time.
The nurse washes their hands as opposed to using hand gel when they notice blood on their palms
opts.why: Visible blood requires soap and water

opts.t: The nurse allows the water to run off their elbows when washing
opts.why: Routine washing should drain toward fingertips, not elbows

ans: EXPECTED ANSWER (not keyed in source): D — Hands should be below elbows during routine washing.

stem: The nurse is caring for a client who has a Clostridium difficile infection. Which of the following cleansing agents should the nurse use for hand hygiene?

opts.t: Nonantimicrobial soap
opts.why: Soap and water physically remove spores

opts.t: Alcohol-based hand rub
opts.why: Alcohol does not reliably kill spores

opts.t: Povidone-iodine
opts.why: Not required for routine spore removal

opts.t: Chlorhexidine

ans: EXPECTED ANSWER (not keyed in source): A — Soap and water remove spores; sanitizer is inadequate.

stem: A client who needs maximum support is ambulating with a cane for the first time. After educating the client on proper ambulation with a cane, you assess how well the client understood the instructions. Which findings below demonstrate the proper technique? (Select all that apply.)

opts.t: The top of the cane should be level with the hip joint.
The client moves the weak leg past the cane while walking.
opts.why: Weak leg advances with cane, not beyond it

opts.t: The arm that is holding the cane is flexed at 40-degrees.
The cane should hold the cane 6 inches in front and 6 inches to the side of the stronger leg.
opts.why: Forward and lateral placement provides support

ans: EXPECTED ANSWER (not keyed in source): A, D — Cane at hip/wrist height, six inches forward and lateral; elbow about 15–30°.

stem: A client who is ambulating with crutches moves both crutches forward along with the injured leg and then moves the non-injured forward. What type of gait did the client use while ambulating with crutches?

opts.t: Three-point gait
opts.why: Both crutches and affected leg move together

opts.t: Swing-to-gait
Four-point gait
opts.why: Four separate points advance in sequence

opts.t: Two-point gait
opts.why: Opposite crutch and foot advance together

ans: EXPECTED ANSWER (not keyed in source): A — Crutches and affected leg advance, then strong leg.

stem: Which of the following qualities does the nurse need to provide caring?

opts.t: Ability to create a trusting environment
Desire to have a stable career and income
opts.why: Personal financial goals are not patient-centered

opts.t: Sensitivity to the needs of other nurses
opts.why: Collegial sensitivity alone does not establish patient trust

opts.t: Longing to help others live a healthy life
opts.why: Desire to help alone does not establish trust

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): A — Trust is central to caring.

stem: Which of the following describes the nurse’s role for an older adult client with a chronic illness?

opts.t: Provide caring to help the client live at the optimal level of health and wellness.
Suggest that the client accept eventual death to reduce the burdens on the client’s family.
Implement an individualized therapeutic regimen that brings about a cure.
opts.why: Chronic illness may not be curable

opts.t: Encourage the client to minimize the use of services to control costs.
opts.why: Cost reduction is not the primary goal

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): A — Optimize wellness, not cure chronic disease.

stem: A 76-year-old is indifferent and responds to others only when they initiate an interaction. What form of group therapy would be most useful to promote resocialization?

opts.t: Psychotherapy
opts.why: Focuses on psychological treatment rather than shared recall

opts.t: Orientation
opts.why: Targets orientation to person, time and place

opts.t: Reminiscence
Activity group
opts.why: May engage clients but is less targeted to life review

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): C — Reminiscence promotes resocialization.

stem: An advance directive gives legally binding direction for health care interventions when a patient

opts.t: has a new diagnosis of cancer.
opts.why: Diagnosis alone does not establish incapacity

opts.t: is diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease.
opts.why: Diagnosis alone does not establish incapacity

opts.t: is unable to make decisions for self because of illness.
opts.why: Directives guide decisions when capacity is lost

opts.t: diagnosed with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is unable to speak.
opts.why: Inability to speak does not imply incapacity

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): C — Directive applies when decision-making capacity is lost.

stem: A nurse is caring for a client who has Parkinson's disease and is taking diphenhydramine 25 mg PO TID. Which of the following therapeutic outcomes should the nurse expect to see?

opts.t: Improved bladder function
Delay in disease progression
Decreased tremors
Relief of depression

ans: EXPECTED ANSWER (not keyed in source): C — Anticholinergic effect may reduce tremors.

stem: A nurse is providing teaching to the family of a client who has Parkinson's disease. Which of the following information should the nurse include in the teaching?

opts.t: Provide client supervision.
Speak loudly to the client.
opts.why: Parkinson disease does not imply hearing loss

opts.t: Limit client physical activity.
Leave the television on continuously.

ans: EXPECTED ANSWER (not keyed in source): A — Supervision promotes safety while preserving independence.

stem: A patient has been admitted after overdosing on acetaminophen. The nurse plans to monitor this patient for development of which complication related to the overdose?

opts.t: Decreased urinary output
opts.why: Renal injury may occur but is not the hallmark

opts.t: Kidney stones
Acute hepatic necrosis
Metabolic alkalosis
opts.why: Acidosis may occur, not typical alkalosis

ans: EXPECTED ANSWER (not keyed in source): C — Acetaminophen overdose can cause hepatic necrosis.

stem: The nurse is preparing to administer an injection of morphine to a patient and notes a respiratory rate of 10 breaths/min. What is the nurse’s best action?

opts.t: Hold the drug, record the assessment, and recheck in 1 hour.
Administer a smaller dose and record the findings.
Notify the health care provider and delay drug administration.
opts.why: Hold opioid and report respiratory depression

opts.t: Administer the prescribed dose and notify the health care provider.

ans: EXPECTED ANSWER (not keyed in source): C — Hold opioid and notify provider for respiratory depression.

stem: A nurse is making a home visit on a new mother with an infant. What action by the mother requires the nurse to intervene?

opts.t: Shows the nurse the water heater setting that is on 110° F (43.3° C)
Keeps hand on infant while reaching for supplies on changing table
Places baby to sleep in crib with no blankets, toys, or other objects
Cooks while holding and cuddling infant to provide comfort
opts.why: Hot food and surfaces threaten burns

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): D — Cooking while holding baby risks burns.

stem: The nurse plans a teaching session with a toddler’s parents on car safety. Which will the nurse teach? (Select all that apply.)

opts.t: Place the car safety seat in the front passenger seat equipped with an airbag.
Place the car safety seat in the rear seat, behind the driver’s seat.
Secure in a rear-facing, upright car safety seat.
opts.why: Rear-face until seat height or weight limit

opts.t: After the age of 2 years, toddlers can be placed in a forward-facing car seat.
opts.why: Source expects this; only transition after rear-facing limits

opts.t: Harness safety straps should fit snugly.
opts.why: Snug harness reduces movement in collision

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): B, C, D, E — Rear seat, rear-facing until size limit, snug harness; forward-facing after rear-facing limit.

stem:
The nurse in the telemetry unit is caring for a 60-year-old client who has a history of several episodes of ventricular tachycardia in the past 48 hours. A normal QT interval was observed earlier today. A left ventricular assist device was inserted 2 weeks ago.
Electrocardiogram:
[image.png](https://classroom.galencollege.edu/courses/8273805/files/359448245/preview)
Select the best option to complete the following sentence.
The nurse should first ___________.

opts.t: check the client’s deep tendon reflexes
asses (collect data about/lpn) the client’s Chvostek and Trousseau signs
hold the client’s next dose of amiodarone
opts.why: Holding a later dose does not treat current rhythm

opts.t: administer magnesium sulfate, 2 g, IV over 2 minutes for the client
opts.why: Source identifies torsades; magnesium treats it

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): D — Source identifies torsades; magnesium is priority.

stem: The nurse is caring for a patient who is receiving a high dose of intravenous azithromycin to treat an infection. The patient is also taking acetaminophen for pain. The nurse should expect to review which lab values when monitoring for this drug’s side effects?

opts.t: Electrolytes
Liver enzymes
Complete blood counts
opts.why: Not primary monitoring for hepatic injury

opts.t: Urinalysis
opts.why: Does not detect liver toxicity directly

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): B — Both drugs may increase hepatic risk.

stem: The nurse provides home-care instructions for a patient who will take a high dose of azithromycin after discharge from the hospital. Which statement by the patient indicates an understanding of the teaching?

opts.t: “I should avoid dairy products while taking this drug.”
opts.why: Dairy avoidance is not routinely required

opts.t: “I should expect diarrhea to be a common, mild side effect.”
opts.why: Diarrhea can occur, but significant or persistent diarrhea needs evaluation

opts.t: “I may take antacids 2 hours before taking this drug.”
opts.why: Separating relevant antacids avoids absorption interaction

opts.t: “I should take acetaminophen for fever or mild pain.”
opts.why: Additional acetaminophen may increase hepatic risk

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): C — Separate antacids by two hours; source rationale.

stem: A nurse is conducting a physical assessment of a 90-year-old client. The nurse understands that special considerations when working with older adults include which of the following?

opts.t: Older adults do not require a “head to toe assessment,” so an abbreviated assessment should be done.
opts.why: Older adults still need comprehensive assessment

opts.t: The nurse needs to leave the assessment that is most painful until the end.
opts.why: Painful assessment need not invariably be last

opts.t: It is important to complete the entire physical assessment at one time, conducting a “head to toe assessment.”
The nurse needs to first direct the assessment to that which is most likely associated with the presenting problem.

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): D — Focus assessment on presenting problem.

stem: Using the Resident Assessment Instrument (RAI), the nurse identifies a trigger for a male nursing home resident who requires an indwelling urinary catheter from the Minimum Data Set (MDS). Which should the nurse do next?

opts.t: Refer to the appropriate quality measures.
Assign suitable nursing interventions.
Institute agency-approved catheter care.
opts.why: Routine catheter care does not investigate trigger

opts.t: Develop an individualized care plan.

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): A — Assess MDS trigger using relevant quality measures before planning.

stem: A nurse hears a colleague tell a nursing student that they never touch a patient unless they are performing a procedure or doing an assessment. From a caring perspective, the nurse tells the student

opts.t: touch is only used when a patient is in pain.
opts.why: Comforting touch is not limited to pain

opts.t: touch forms a connection between nurse and patient.
touch is a type of verbal communication.
they do not touch the patients either.

ans: EXPECTED ANSWER (not keyed in source): B — Therapeutic touch creates connection.

stem: A nurse completing a hospital discharge to home understands that which of the following interventions is most important before discharge?

opts.t: Medication reconciliation
Contacting a durable medical equipment facility
Providing a list of community resources
Educating the client on appropriate range-of-motion exercises

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): A — Reconcile medications before discharge.

stem: Which of the following statements are true about long-term care? (Select all that apply.)

opts.t: Most long-term care is paid for by Medicare.
opts.why: Medicare generally does not cover custodial long-term care

opts.t: The number of older adults needing long-term care services is expected to increase 233%.
Costs of long-term care have outpaced inflation since 2003.
Long-term care is the most cost-effective manner in which to care for older adults.
opts.why: Cost-effectiveness depends on setting and need

opts.t: Most individuals in the United States have purchased long-term care insurance.
opts.why: Most people lack dedicated long-term care insurance

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): B, C — Source describes increasing demand and cost (historical figures).

stem: The nurse is concerned that a break in sterile procedure has occured.  Which of the following actions would caused a break in sterile field?

opts.t: Grasping the edge of the outermost flap and opening it away from oneself
opts.why: Opening away avoids reaching over field

opts.t: Keeping objects on the field 1 inch from the edge
opts.why: Keep items outside the contaminated border

opts.t: Keeping the sterile field in eyesight
Transferring a sterile object to a sterile field with a clean gloved hand

ans: EXPECTED ANSWER (not keyed in source): D — Clean gloves are not sterile.

stem: A nurse is performing a sterile dressing change for a client.  Which of the following actions by the nurse would compromise the sterility of the procedure? (Select all that apply.)

opts.t: The nurse leans across the sterile field.
The nurse turning their back on the sterile field.
Opening a sterile package and then dropping the item onto a non-sterile field.
The nurse opens a sterile package and drops a sterile item in the one inch border around the field.

ans: EXPECTED ANSWER (not keyed in source): A, B, C, D — Reaching, turning away, nonsterile surfaces and border contaminate.

stem: A patient who takes a diuretic and a b-blocker to control blood pressure is scheduled for breast reconstruction surgery. Which patient information is most important to communicate to the health care provider before surgery?

opts.t: Hematocrit 36%
Pulse rate 58 beats/minute
opts.why: Beta blockers may explain mild bradycardia

opts.t: Blood pressure 144/82
Serum potassium 3.2 mEq/L
opts.why: Low potassium raises perioperative arrhythmia risk

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): D — Hypokalemia increases dysrhythmia risk.

stem: A client with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) is scheduled for hemodialysis in one hour.  The nurse should notify the primary health care provider that the client has a

opts.t: Sodium 145 mEq/L
Creatinine 3.5 mg/dl
Potassium 6.8 mEq/L
BUN of 60 mg/dl

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): C — Severe hyperkalemia threatens cardiac conduction.

stem: As the nurse you are providing care for a client who is 2 days post-op and has still not had a bowel movement nor have they passed flatus.  On assessment, you note the abdomen is distended and no bowel sounds are noted in the four quadrants. You notify the MD. What non-invasive nursing interventions can you perform without a MD order?

opts.t: Encourage at least 3000 mL of fluids per day
opts.why: Oral fluids inappropriate with suspected ileus

opts.t: Encourage ambulation, maintain NPO status, and monitor intake and output
opts.why: NPO, mobility and I&O are supportive measures

opts.t: Administer IV fluids
Insert a nasogastric attached to intermittent suction

ans: EXPECTED ANSWER (not keyed in source): B — Suspected ileus: NPO, ambulate if safe, track I&O.

stem: A nurse is developing a care plan for a patient who is at risk for developing pneumonia after surgery. Which of the following are appropriate nursing interventions? (Select all that apply.)

opts.t: Encourage early ambulation and patient to eat meals in beside chair
Encourage patient intake of 3000 ml/day of fluids if not contraindicated
opts.why: Hydration helps clear secretions if allowed

opts.t: Encourage patient to use the incentive spirometer device 10 times every 1-2 hours while awake
Repositioning every 3-4 hours

ans: EXPECTED ANSWER (not keyed in source): A, B, C — Mobilization, hydration if permitted, incentive spirometry.

stem: A patient who will begin oxygen therapy has a history of sinus disorders. This patient would benefit most from which oxygen setup?

opts.t: High oxygen flow rate
A humidifier
A nasal cannula
A Venturi mask
opts.why: Precise oxygen delivery does not address dryness

ans: EXPECTED ANSWER (not keyed in source): B — Humidification reduces mucosal drying.

stem: The nurse loosens mucus plugs by using percussion on a patient over the area of the

opts.t: thorax
spine between the scapulae
sternum
midaxillary line on the rib cage
opts.why: Specific location depends on affected lung segment

ans: EXPECTED ANSWER (not keyed in source): A — Percuss thorax over lung fields, not bony prominences.

stem: Which of the following nursing diagnosis would the nurse expect to assign for a client with diabetes insipidus ?

opts.t: excess fluid volume related to intake greater than output.
opts.why: DI causes water loss, not retention

opts.t: risk for impaired skin integrity related to generalized edema.
sleep pattern disturbance related to frequent waking to void.
impaired gas exchange related to fluid retention in lungs.
opts.why: Pulmonary fluid retention is not characteristic

ans: EXPECTED ANSWER (not keyed in source): C — Polyuria disrupts sleep.

stem: Which assessment finding for a client admitted with Graves’ disease requires the most rapid intervention by the nurse?

opts.t: Heart rate 126 beats/minute
Blood pressure 166/98 mm Hg
Abdominal pain with nausea
opts.why: GI symptoms may occur but fever is more alarming

opts.t: Temperature 103.8° F (40.4° C)

ans: EXPECTED ANSWER (not keyed in source): D — High fever suggests thyroid storm.

stem: The nurse is caring for a 63-year-old with Cushing’s who is scheduled for a computed tomography (CT) scan with contrast. Which information about the client is most important to discuss with the health care provider before the test?

opts.t: Recent history of paralytic ilieus
opts.why: Less directly related to contrast safety

opts.t: History of renal insufficiency
Complains of chronic headache
Blood glucose level of 224 mg/dL
opts.why: Hyperglycemia needs monitoring but renal status is more relevant

ans: EXPECTED ANSWER (not keyed in source): B — Renal insufficiency raises contrast-associated kidney risk.

stem: The nurse in the inpatient psychiatric unit is caring for a 26-year-old client who has bipolar I disorder and is receiving prescribed carbamazepine. The nurse should first _____.

opts.t: question the client about suicidal thoughts
review the client’s serum carbamazepine level
opts.why: Drug levels are important but secondary to safety

opts.t: weigh the client
check the client for urinary retention
opts.why: Retention assessment is not the priority

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): A — Assess suicide risk first.

stem: An emergency code was called after a patient pulled a knife from a pocket and threatened, “I will kill anyone who tries to get near me.” The patient was safely disarmed and placed in seclusion. Justification for use of seclusion was that the patient

opts.t: was threatening to others.
opts.why: Threats alone do not always justify seclusion

opts.t: presented a clear and present danger to others.
presented an undeniable escape risk.
was experiencing psychosis.

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): B — Immediate danger justifies seclusion.

stem: An emergency department nurse realizes that the spouse of a patient is becoming increasingly irritable while waiting. Which intervention should the nurse use to prevent further escalation of the spouse’s anger?

opts.t: Offer the waiting spouse a cup of coffee.
Periodically provide an update and progress report on the patient.
Explain that the patient’s condition is not life threatening.
Suggest that the spouse return home until the patient’s treatment is complete.

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): B — Regular updates reduce uncertainty and escalation.

stem: A patient undergoing diagnostic tests says, “Nothing is wrong with me except a stubborn chest cold.” The spouse reports the patient smokes, coughs daily, lost 15 pounds, and is easily fatigued. Which defense mechanism is the patient using?

opts.t: Projection
opts.why: Projection attributes own feelings to others

opts.t: Denial
Displacement
Regression

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): B — Denial blocks threatening reality.

stem: A nurse assesses a patient with a tentative diagnosis of generalized anxiety disorder. Which question would be most appropriate for the nurse to ask?

opts.t: “Do you find it difficult to control your worrying?”
“Do you feel especially uncomfortable in social situations involving people?”
“Have you been a victim of a crime or seen someone badly injured or killed?”
“Do you repeatedly do certain things over and over again?”

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): A — GAD features uncontrollable worry.

stem: A nurse assesses a patient who takes lithium. Which findings demonstrate evidence of complications?

opts.t: Ascites, dyspnea, and edema
Pharyngitis, mydriasis, and dystonia
opts.why: Not the typical lithium toxicity pattern

opts.t: Alopecia, purpura, and drowsiness
Diaphoresis, weakness, and nausea
opts.why: GI symptoms and weakness suggest toxicity

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): D — Weakness, sweating, nausea suggest lithium toxicity.

stem: A person was online continuously for over 24 hours, posting rhymes on official government websites and inviting politicians to join social networks. The person has not slept or eaten for 3 days. What features of mania are evident?

opts.t: Increased muscle tension and anxiety
Poor judgment and hyperactivity
opts.why: Prolonged activity and risky posting indicate mania

opts.t: Cognitive deficits and paranoia
opts.why: Paranoia is not established by the stem

opts.t: Vegetative signs and poor grooming

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): B — Mania features hyperactivity and impaired judgment.

stem: What feelings are most commonly experienced by nurses working with abusive families?

opts.t: Unconcern for the victim and dislike for the abuser
Outrage toward the victim and discouragement regarding the abuser
opts.why: Anger toward victims is not the expected response

opts.t: Vulnerability for self and empathy with the abuser
opts.why: Not the common pattern identified by source

opts.t: Helplessness regarding the victim and anger toward the abuser

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): D — Helplessness for victim, anger toward abuser.

stem: An adult tells the nurse, “My partner abuses me when I make mistakes, but I always get an apology and a gift afterward. I’ve considered leaving but haven’t been able to bring myself to actually do it.” Which phase in the cycle of violence prevents this adult from leaving?

opts.t: Tension-building
Honeymoon
Acute battering
Stabilization
opts.why: Not the named phase in this model

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): B — Remorse and gifts characterize honeymoon phase.

stem: A patient is seen in the clinic for superficial cuts on both wrists. Initially the patient paces and sobs but after a few minutes, the patient is calmer. The nurse attempts to determine the patient’s perception of the precipitating event by asking:

opts.t: “What was happening when you started feeling this way?”
“Tell me why you were crying.”
“How can I help you feel more comfortable?”
opts.why: Focuses on comfort rather than the trigger

opts.t: “How did your wrists get injured?”

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): A — Identify precipitating event using open question.

stem: After celebrating the fortieth birthday, an individual becomes concerned with the loss of youthful appearance. What type of crisis has occurred?

opts.t: Situational
opts.why: Usually results from an unexpected external event

opts.t: Reactive
Maturational
Body image
opts.why: Describes concern but not the crisis type

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): C — Developmental transition creates maturational crisis.

stem: A patient being treated for depression has taken sertraline daily for a year. The patient calls the clinic nurse and says, “I stopped taking my antidepressant 2 days ago. Now I am having nausea, nervous feelings, and I can’t sleep.” The nurse will advise the patient to:

opts.t: “Take a dose of your antidepressant now and come to the clinic to see the health care provider.”
opts.why: Source expects resumption and clinical review; confirm with prescriber

opts.t: “Resume taking your antidepressants for 2 more weeks and then discontinue them again.”
opts.why: Repeats abrupt discontinuation without a plan

opts.t: “Do not to be alarmed. Take two aspirin and drink plenty of fluids.”
“Go to the nearest emergency department immediately.”
opts.why: Not necessarily an emergency absent severe symptoms

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): A — Abrupt SSRI cessation can produce discontinuation symptoms; contact provider.

stem: A patient diagnosed with depressive disorder begins selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) antidepressant therapy. The nurse should provide information to the patient and family about

opts.t: restricting sodium intake to 1 gram daily.
reporting increased suicidal thoughts.
opts.why: Early treatment requires monitoring suicide risk

opts.t: minimizing exposure to bright sunlight.
maintaining a tyramine-free diet.

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): B — Monitor worsening suicidal thoughts early in treatment.

stem: Which medication should the nurse be concerned about for a client taking fluoxetine?

opts.t: Multivitamins
Diuretics
opts.why: Can increase hyponatremia risk, but source prioritizes bleeding

opts.t: Anticoagulants
Acetaminophen
opts.why: Does not have the same antiplatelet interaction

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): C — SSRIs increase bleeding risk with anticoagulants.

stem: A widower tells friends, “I am taking my neighbor out for dinner. It’s time for me to be more sociable again.” Considering the stages of grief described by Kübler-Ross, which stage is evident?

opts.t: Acceptance
Denial
Anger
Depression
opts.why: Shows renewed interest rather than withdrawal

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): A — Renewed interest suggests acceptance.

stem: A wife received news that her husband died of heart failure and called her family to come to the hospital. She angrily tells the nurse who cared for him, “He would still be alive if you had given him your undivided attention.” Select the nurse’s most therapeutic action.

opts.t: Hold the spouse’s hand in silence until the family arrives.
opts.why: Silent touch may be supportive but does not explicitly acknowledge feelings

opts.t: Say, “Your husband’s heart was so severely damaged that it could no longer pump.”
Say, “I understand you are feeling upset. I will stay with you until your family comes.”
Say, “I will call my supervisor to discuss this matter with you.”
opts.why: Shifts interaction away from emotional support

ans: ANSWER (source rationale available): C — Validate distress and offer presence.

stem: Which of the following would be assessed as a negative symptom of schizophrenia?

opts.t: Anhedonia
opts.why: Loss of pleasure is diminished normal function

opts.t: Agitation

stem: The nurse is caring for a client who sustained a cervical spinal cord injury and had halo traction therapy applied 1 day ago.  Which of the following should the nurse include in the care plan?
